nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Sr-CoSe₂-w nanobelts
nodes.procedure: The Sr-CoSe₂-w nanobelts were synthesized as pre-catalysts by a facile hydrothermal method. In brief, 247.1 mg of Co(AC)₂·4H₂O, 1.62 mg of Sr(AC)₂, and 173 mg of Na₂SeO₃ were dispersed in 40 mL of mixed solution containing DETA and DI water with a volume ratio of 2:1. The mixture was heated to 180°C for 16 h to obtain the 1.0% Sr-CoSe₂-w samples. Sr/Co atomic ratios were controlled by varying the amount of two precursors without changing other conditions. Specifically, 249 mg of Co(AC)₂·4H₂O for pure CoSe₂, 248.7 mg of Co(AC)₂·4H₂O and 0.32 mg of Sr(AC)₂ for 0.2% Sr-CoSe₂-w, 247.8 mg of Co(AC)₂·4H₂O and 0.97 mg of Sr(AC)₂ for 0.6% Sr-CoSe₂-w.

nodes.name: Electrochemical reconstruction of Sr-CoOOH_v nanosheets
nodes.procedure: Electrochemical reconstruction of selenide pre-catalysts (pure CoSe₂, 0.2% Sr-CoSe₂-w, 0.6% Sr-CoSe₂-w, 1.0% Sr-CoSe₂-w) in O₂-saturated 1 M KOH solution via cyclic voltammetry cycling between 1.02 and 1.5 V (vs. RHE) at 50 mV s⁻¹ for 40 cycles, followed by washing with DI water and ethanol to obtain Sr-CoOOH_v nanosheets.

unit_operations.name: Cyclic voltammetry reconstruction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: electrochemical reconstruction of selenide pre-catalysts in O₂-saturated 1 M KOH solution via a typical cyclic voltammetry cycling method between 1.02 and 1.5 V (vs. RHE) with a sweep rate of 50 mVs⁻¹ and forty potential cycles

nodes.characterization_summary: Sr-CoSe2-w nanobelts show smooth and belt-like morphology with uniform distribution of Co, Se, and Sr.
nodes.evidence_snippet: These selenides possessed smooth and belt-like morphology with uniform distribution of Co, Se, and Sr, as identified by transmission electron microscopy (TEM, Fig. 1b)

properties.description: High-resolution image showing sheet-like nanostructures with layered, crumpled morphology and edges

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM with elemental mapping confirms uniform distribution of Co, Se, and Sr in Sr-CoSe2-w nanobelts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) with elemental mapping (Fig. 1c)

nodes.characterization_summary: Sr/Co molar ratio determined as 1.0% in Sr-CoSe2-w by ICP-OES.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Sr/Co molar ratio was determined as 1.0% by inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES)

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM confirms well-maintained cubic CoSe2 structure of 1.0% Sr-CoSe2-w with Sr-ion substitution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM image clearly suggested the well-maintained cubic CoSe2 structure of 1.0% Sr-CoSe2-w

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier-transformed EXAFS shows reduced Co-Se coordination from 3.9 to 2.3 and increased Co-Se bond length after Sr substitution in Sr-CoSe2-w.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier-transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra and fitting results demonstrated the largely reduced Co-Se coordination from 3.9 for pure CoSe2 to 2.3 for 1.0% Sr-CoSe2-w

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p XPS shows peaks at 778.5 eV and 793.4 eV for Co-Se bond with negative shift indicating enriched valence-electron density after Sr substitution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co 2p X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectrum for 1.0% Sr-CoSe2-w exhibited two typical peaks at 778.5 eV and 793.4 eV that assigned to Co-Se bond

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman analysis during potential cycles shows disappearance of CoSe2 peaks (476, 517, 683 cm⁻¹) and emergence of CoOOH Eg and A1g modes at 498 and 594 cm⁻¹, with accelerated reconstruction for Sr-substituted pre-catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2b, the Raman spectra of pristine 1.0% Sr-CoSe2 w pre-catalysts showcased three typical peaks at 476, 517 and 683 cm⁻¹ assigned to cubic CoSe2 phase. As the potential cycles proceeded, these peaks tended to vanish, together with the formation of another two peaks at 498 and 594 cm⁻¹ assigned to Eg and A1g vibrational modes of Co-O in CoOOH

nodes.characterization_summary: Reconstructed Sr-CoOOH_v shows interconnected nanosheets with massive boundaries.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of reconstructed oxyhydroxides was characterized by TEM (Fig. 2d), where interconnected nanosheets with massive boundaries were observed

nodes.characterization_summary: Sr/Co ratio maintained as 1.0% in Sr-CoOOH_v nanosheets by ICP-OES.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Sr/Co ratio was maintained as 1.0% by ICP-OES

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM visualizes substituted Sr atoms (bright spots) and amorphous structure confirmed by SAED diffraction rings in Sr-CoOOH_v.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic structure was further visualized by aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM image (Fig. 2f). The bright spots marked by yellow circles clearly suggested the substituted Sr atoms

nodes.characterization_summary: Sr K-edge EXAFS shows absence of Sr-Sr coordination confirming atomic dispersion of Sr atoms in Sr-CoOOH_v.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic dispersion of these Sr atoms could also be verified by the absence of Sr-Sr coordination in Sr K-edge EXAFS spectra (Fig. 2g)

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge EXAFS shows Co-O at 1.5 Å and Co-Co at 2.5 Å; Co-O bond length shrinks and Co-Co coordination numbers decrease from 3.0 (CoOOH) to 2.4 (1.0% Sr-CoOOH_v) indicating Co vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: All the Sr-CoOOH_v nanosheets exhibited two main peaks at around 1.5 Å and 2.5 Å attributing to Co-O and Co-Co bonds for CoOOH, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p3/2 XPS peaks at 779.9 eV and 781.1 eV for Co³⁺ with positive shift; Sr 3d peaks at 133.4 and 135.1 eV show negative shift indicating enhanced Co-O covalency in Sr-CoOOH_v.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Co2p3/2 XPS peaks at 779.9 eV and 781.1 eV corresponded to the Co3+ cations in CoOOH

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS shows increased O-Co bonds (529.7 eV), decreased OH-Co bonds (530.8 eV), and increased adsorbed water from pure CoOOH to 1.0% Sr-CoOOH_v.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron state of O sites was studied by O 1s XPS spectra, which could be fitted into four contributions from O-Co bonds (529.7 eV), OH-Co bonds (530.8 eV)

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES shows gradual elevation of Co oxidation state to ~3 during reconstruction from Sr-CoSe2-w to Sr-CoOOH_v.
nodes.evidence_snippet: together with the gradually elevated Co oxidation state to ~3 (Fig. 2c), manifesting the complete reconstruction from selenide to oxyhydroxide phase

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns confirm amorphous structure of reconstructed Sr-CoOOH_v nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Similar morphology and amorphous structures were also observed in other reconstructed Sr-CoOOH_v nanosheets... as evidenced by the TEM images, HRTEM images, XRD patterns and ICP-OES analysis (Supplementary Fig. 7,8)

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images confirm amorphous structure of reconstructed Sr-CoOOH_v nanosheets.
